value: Civil Code (BGB), tenancy chapter, §§ 535 ff. Residential rent rules including deposit, rent increases and termination are in the BGB.
Security may not exceed three times the monthly rent, excluding service charges paid as a flat rate or advance (§ 551(1) BGB).

Landlord must invest a cash deposit with a bank at the rate usual for savings deposits with three months notice, separate from the landlord's own assets; the tenant may pay in three equal monthly instalments (§ 551(2)-(3) BGB).

Landlord may ask for consent to a rise up to the local comparative rent if the rent has been unchanged for 15 months; the request may be made at the earliest one year after the last increase (§ 558(1) BGB).

Rent may not rise by more than 20 percent within three years (15 percent in areas designated by Land governments as having endangered housing supply), excluding modernisation and service-charge changes (§ 558(3) BGB).

field: Rent at start of tenancy in tight markets
value: In areas with a tight housing market designated by a Land ordinance, rent at the start of a tenancy may exceed the local comparative rent by at most 10 percent (§ 556d(1) BGB). Designations are made by each Land, so they differ by municipality.

Landlord may terminate only with a legitimate interest (e.g. tenant breach, own use) and not to raise rent (§ 573 BGB). Notice is three months, extended by three months after five and again after eight years of tenancy (§ 573c BGB).

An energy certificate must be issued when a building or dwelling is let, unless a valid one already exists (§ 80(3) of the Building Energy Act; the official page shows the act under the title Gebäudemodernisierungsgesetz - GModG).

value: Tenant: at least one month written notice for agreements up to 10 years. Lessor: at least one month for arrears or unauthorised occupancy and for demolition or reconstruction where the agreement is up to one year; at least three months where the agreement is one to three years (Section 27).

value: Private Residential Leases Act (Cap. 604).

All private residential lease contracts entered into after the Act's entry into force, including renewals, must be registered; unregistered contracts are null and void. The lessor must register the contract with the Authority within 30 days of the start of the lease (art. 4).
A long private residential lease cannot have a duration of less than one year; an agreement stipulating a shorter duration is deemed agreed for at least one year (art. 8).

Rent increases may take place only once every year. Without an express agreement the rent cannot be revised during the term. Yearly increases may not exceed the annual variation of the Property Price Index published by the National Statistics Office (average of the previous four quarters), and may never exceed the previous rent by more than five percent; a negative variation does not reduce rent (art. 14).

note: No cap found in the Act text read; the Act allows the lessor to request a security amount (art. 6(1)(f)). Left blank.

value: Civil Code (Act No. 40/1964 Coll.), lease of flats (§ 685 and following).
source_publisher: Slov-Lex (Ministry of Justice of the Slovak Republic)
note: Text is in Slovak; the summary is ours. Version of 1 January 2026.

value: The lease contract must state the object and extent of use, the rent and the payment for services linked to use of the flat (or how they are calculated); if the contract was not made in writing, a record of its content is drawn up. If no duration is agreed, the lease is presumed concluded for an indefinite period (§ 686).
source_publisher: Slov-Lex (Ministry of Justice of the Slovak Republic)
note: Text is in Slovak; the summary is ours. Version of 1 January 2026.

value: How rent and service charges are calculated and paid, and the cases in which the landlord may unilaterally increase rent, are set by a separate legal regulation (§ 696(1)).
source_publisher: Slov-Lex (Ministry of Justice of the Slovak Republic)
note: Text is in Slovak; the summary is ours. Version of 1 January 2026.

value: A tenant who does not pay rent or service charges within five days of the due date must pay the landlord a late-payment fee (§ 697).
source_publisher: Slov-Lex (Ministry of Justice of the Slovak Republic)
note: Text is in Slovak; the summary is ours. Version of 1 January 2026.

value: A flat lease ends by written agreement or written notice; the notice period is three months, starting on the first day of the month after delivery, and the landlord may set a longer period in writing. For notice given for non-payment where the tenant proves objective material hardship, a six-month protection period is added (§ 710(1), (3), (4)).
source_publisher: Slov-Lex (Ministry of Justice of the Slovak Republic)
note: Text is in Slovak; the summary is ours. Version of 1 January 2026.

value: The landlord may give notice if, among other grounds, the landlord needs the flat for self or close relatives, or the tenant grossly breaches duties, for example by not paying rent or service charges for more than three months or sub-letting without written consent (§ 711(1)).
source_publisher: Slov-Lex (Ministry of Justice of the Slovak Republic)
note: Text is in Slovak; the summary is ours. Version of 1 January 2026.

value: Property Rent Law, Law No. 27 of 2014 (in force six months after publication in the Official Gazette).
source_publisher: Legislation and Legal Opinion Commission (Kingdom of Bahrain)
note: English text of Law No. 27 of 2014 on the site of the official legislation commission; the document carries a note that the official version is the Arabic one in the Official Gazette.

value: Lease agreements within the scope of the Law must be in writing and registered, with any later alterations, within one month of conclusion; the fact of leasing may be proven by all methods of evidence (Art. 3). Registration fee is set by ministerial order and is borne by the lessor (Art. 7).
source_publisher: Legislation and Legal Opinion Commission (Kingdom of Bahrain)
note: English text of Law No. 27 of 2014 on the site of the official legislation commission; the document carries a note that the official version is the Arabic one in the Official Gazette.

value: A lease concluded without an agreed period, or whose period cannot be proven, is treated as concluded for the rent-payment period (Art. 4(A)).
source_publisher: Legislation and Legal Opinion Commission (Kingdom of Bahrain)
note: English text of Law No. 27 of 2014 on the site of the official legislation commission; the document carries a note that the official version is the Arabic one in the Official Gazette.

value: The lessor may not increase rent until two years from the lease start or the last increase; the increase is 5% for residential use and 7% for commercial, industrial and other uses, at most five times during the lease, unless otherwise agreed in writing (Art. 27(a)).
source_publisher: Legislation and Legal Opinion Commission (Kingdom of Bahrain)
note: English text of Law No. 27 of 2014 on the site of the official legislation commission; the document carries a note that the official version is the Arabic one in the Official Gazette.

value: The lessor must notify the tenant of the intended increase by registered letter at least three months before the end of the second year, unless otherwise agreed (Art. 27(c)).
source_publisher: Legislation and Legal Opinion Commission (Kingdom of Bahrain)
note: English text of Law No. 27 of 2014 on the site of the official legislation commission; the document carries a note that the official version is the Arabic one in the Official Gazette.

value: A tenant who wishes to vacate must notify the lessor by registered letter at least three months before the expiry date (Art. 34(b)).
source_publisher: Legislation and Legal Opinion Commission (Kingdom of Bahrain)
note: English text of Law No. 27 of 2014 on the site of the official legislation commission; the document carries a note that the official version is the Arabic one in the Official Gazette.

value: If the term expires and the tenant stays with the lessor's knowledge and without objection, the lease is treated as extended for a similar period on the same conditions (Art. 34(a)).
source_publisher: Legislation and Legal Opinion Commission (Kingdom of Bahrain)
note: English text of Law No. 27 of 2014 on the site of the official legislation commission; the document carries a note that the official version is the Arabic one in the Official Gazette.

value: A lease does not end on the death of the lessor or tenant; the tenant's heirs may request termination within one year of the death (Art. 36(a)).
source_publisher: Legislation and Legal Opinion Commission (Kingdom of Bahrain)
note: English text of Law No. 27 of 2014 on the site of the official legislation commission; the document carries a note that the official version is the Arabic one in the Official Gazette.

value: Provisions regulating the relationship between landlords and tenants of residences and commercial and industrial premises, annexed to Royal Decree 6/89, as amended up to Royal Decree 12/2025 (in force from 13 July 2025).
note: Arabic text, amended up to Royal Decree 12/2025; the summary is ours.

value: A lease that is not registered, with the fee paid, within one month of conclusion cannot be relied on before any official body in Oman, and a fine of three times the fee, calculated on rent due for the delay period, applies (Art. 4).
note: Arabic text, amended up to Royal Decree 12/2025; the summary is ours.

value: The landlord may not increase rent of residential, commercial or industrial premises until three years have passed from the lease start or from the last agreed increase, unless agreed otherwise (Art. 6). The provision as read sets no percentage cap.
note: Arabic text, amended up to Royal Decree 12/2025; the summary is ours.

value: The landlord may increase rent at any time if the tenant requested improvements or additions and the landlord carried them out; the increase must be proportionate to their cost (Art. 6).
note: Arabic text, amended up to Royal Decree 12/2025; the summary is ours.

value: For residential premises the landlord may not ask the tenant to vacate within three years of the lease start (five years for commercial, professional or industrial use), unless agreed otherwise; after the term the landlord who does not want to renew must notify the tenant at least three months before the term ends (Art. 6 bis).
note: Arabic text, amended up to Royal Decree 12/2025; the summary is ours.

value: The lease runs to the agreed end and renews automatically during the period in which the landlord cannot seek eviction, unless the tenant notifies the landlord in writing of a wish to vacate at least three months before the term ends (Art. 6 bis (1)).
note: Arabic text, amended up to Royal Decree 12/2025; the summary is ours.

value: Before the end of the term the landlord may seek eviction where rent is not paid within fifteen days of its due date; eviction is not ordered if the tenant pays before the decision (Art. 7).
note: Arabic text, amended up to Royal Decree 12/2025; the summary is ours.

value: The tenant may not assign the lease or sub-let without the landlord's written consent (Art. 5).
note: Arabic text, amended up to Royal Decree 12/2025; the summary is ours.

value: Civil Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan, property lease provisions (Art. 675 and following), including special rules for lease of residential rooms.
source_publisher: Official Legal Acts Database of the Republic of Azerbaijan (e-qanun.az, Ministry of Justice)
note: Civil Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan (text in Azerbaijani; the summary is ours). Applies to leases of residential rooms and other property.

value: A lease of a residential room may be terminated only by notice given on the first working day of a calendar month, taking effect at the end of the following month; notice must be in writing and state the grounds (Arts. 690.1, 690.2, 691.2). The text extends the notice periods in the tenant's favour by three months after three, six and nine years of occupation (Art. 691.3).
source_publisher: Official Legal Acts Database of the Republic of Azerbaijan (e-qanun.az, Ministry of Justice)
note: Civil Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan (text in Azerbaijani; the summary is ours). Applies to leases of residential rooms and other property.

value: For a residential room the landlord may terminate only where there is a substantial interest, for example the tenant is at fault for breaching contract obligations or the landlord needs the room as a home for self or family members (Art. 692.1, 692.2). An agreement allowing the landlord to terminate immediately on grounds other than those in law has no effect (Art. 687).
source_publisher: Official Legal Acts Database of the Republic of Azerbaijan (e-qanun.az, Ministry of Justice)
note: Civil Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan (text in Azerbaijani; the summary is ours). Applies to leases of residential rooms and other property.

value: Where the tenant must give security for performance of the lease, it may not exceed twice the monthly rent; cash security must be kept by the landlord separately from own assets in a bank at the interest usual for savings deposits, the interest belonging to the tenant (Art. 688.2). For residential rooms an agreement departing from this to the tenant's detriment has no effect (Art. 688.3).
source_publisher: Official Legal Acts Database of the Republic of Azerbaijan (e-qanun.az, Ministry of Justice)
note: Civil Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan (text in Azerbaijani; the summary is ours). Applies to leases of residential rooms and other property. The Article refers to security for performance of obligations; wording as published.

value: A reservation payment made to the landlord before the lease is credited against rent when the lease is concluded; the part exceeding two months of rent can be reclaimed by the person at any time (Art. 688.1). A landlord of a residential room cannot validly agree a forfeit-type payment from the tenant (Art. 688.4).
source_publisher: Official Legal Acts Database of the Republic of Azerbaijan (e-qanun.az, Ministry of Justice)
note: Civil Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan (text in Azerbaijani; the summary is ours). Applies to leases of residential rooms and other property.

value: Where the lease term is longer than one month, rent is paid in instalments at the end of each month; rent set by periods is paid at the end of each period (Art. 684.1).
source_publisher: Official Legal Acts Database of the Republic of Azerbaijan (e-qanun.az, Ministry of Justice)
note: Civil Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan (text in Azerbaijani; the summary is ours). Applies to leases of residential rooms and other property.

value: Civil Code of the Republic of Armenia, residential premises lease contract (Arts. 660-676).
source_publisher: ARLIS - Legal Information System of Armenia (official text)
note: Civil Code of the Republic of Armenia, English text with changes up to HO-394-N of 24 October 2024.

value: The residential lease must be in writing as a single document signed by the parties, is subject to notary certification, and the rights arising from it are subject to state registration (Arts. 662, 663).
source_publisher: ARLIS - Legal Information System of Armenia (official text)
note: Civil Code of the Republic of Armenia, English text with changes up to HO-394-N of 24 October 2024.

value: The lease is concluded for the term set by the contract; if no term is set it is treated as concluded for an indefinite term (Art. 672).
source_publisher: ARLIS - Legal Information System of Armenia (official text)
note: Civil Code of the Republic of Armenia, English text with changes up to HO-394-N of 24 October 2024.

value: Rent is set by agreement of the parties; unilateral change is not allowed except in cases provided for by law or the contract (Art. 671(1), (2)). Rent is paid monthly unless the contract provides otherwise (Art. 671(3)).
source_publisher: ARLIS - Legal Information System of Armenia (official text)
note: Civil Code of the Republic of Armenia, English text with changes up to HO-394-N of 24 October 2024.

value: The tenant and other citizens permanently residing with the tenant may, by common consent, terminate the lease by giving the lessor three months' notice (Art. 675(1)).
source_publisher: ARLIS - Legal Information System of Armenia (official text)
note: Civil Code of the Republic of Armenia, English text with changes up to HO-394-N of 24 October 2024.

value: The lessor may terminate only through court, for example where the tenant fails to pay rent more than twice after the payment term, or the tenant or persons they are responsible for destroyed or damaged the premises; eviction follows a court judgment (Arts. 675(2), 676).
source_publisher: ARLIS - Legal Information System of Armenia (official text)
note: Civil Code of the Republic of Armenia, English text with changes up to HO-394-N of 24 October 2024.

value: Transfer of ownership of the let premises is not a ground to rescind or alter the lease; the new owner becomes the lessor on the existing terms unless law provides otherwise (Art. 664).
source_publisher: ARLIS - Legal Information System of Armenia (official text)
note: Civil Code of the Republic of Armenia, English text with changes up to HO-394-N of 24 October 2024.

value: Maintenance repair is the tenant's duty and major repair is the lessor's duty, unless the contract provides otherwise (Art. 670).
source_publisher: ARLIS - Legal Information System of Armenia (official text)
note: Civil Code of the Republic of Armenia, English text with changes up to HO-394-N of 24 October 2024.

value: Sub-letting is allowed with the lessor's consent; the sub-lease cannot exceed the main lease term (Art. 673).
source_publisher: ARLIS - Legal Information System of Armenia (official text)
note: Civil Code of the Republic of Armenia, English text with changes up to HO-394-N of 24 October 2024.
